title: Integer multiplicity is a local property (T4) and passes to domain restrictions
statement: Assume (REP), (MR) and (IMC). Here (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO) denote the exact frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, cmc_slice_mass_bounds, cmc_deformation_theorem and dtc_vanish_off_support; they are not available in this child's environment, so the needed ones appear verbatim as hypotheses of the Lean statement and are discharged by the parent proof. In words: (REP) a current with locally finite mass in an open U has a mass representation (μ, ξ) (μ(W) = M_W for open W, μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0, μ finite on compacts of U, |ξ| ≤ 1, X(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, and μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 if also the boundary has locally finite mass); (MR) M_W(X) = R.measure(W) for an IMRep R of X and open W; (IMC) (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces for nested Borel sets, (b) the restriction of an IMRep to a Borel set is an IMRep of some current, (c) differences of IM currents are IM, (d) IMRep orientations satisfy |orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e.; (SL) slicing by an L-Lipschitz f of a current represented together with its boundary, with Z_t := ∂(X⌞{f<t}) − (∂X)⌞{f<t} vanishing on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(Z_t) ≤ L liminf_h h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h<f<t}) and the integrated bound; (DT) the deformation theorem with its mass and support bounds; (VO) a current vanishes on test forms whose support misses its support. Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and X ∈ 𝒟_k(U). (1) If M_W(X) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure in U, and every x ∈ U has r > 0 with B_r(x) ⊆ U such that the domain restriction X|_{B_r(x)} ∈ 𝒟_k(B_r(x)) (X.restrictDomain) is integer multiplicity, then X is integer multiplicity. (2) If V ⊆ U is open and X is integer multiplicity, then X|_V ∈ 𝒟_k(V) is integer multiplicity.
